attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 27 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder already keeps on the Romanian calendar, and the entry is plainly the same man: the first of the seven deacons, the first martyr, stoned outside the city. The page glosses his name, «ΣΤΕΦΑΝΟΣ (από το στέφανος) = ο αθλοφόρος, ο άξιος στεφάνου νίκης», and names Σκύδρα as the town that holds him patron — not drafted as a location, since no coordinate is proposed for a patronage. It gives no year at all, so the folder's dateless state is unchanged. It prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name him and are taken; its megalynarion, its oikos and its two kathismata are not kinds this schema holds and are left. It closes by naming «Ανακομιδή του Ιερού Λειψάνου του Αγίου Πρωτομάρτυρα Στεφάνου», the translation of his relic, which is a separate commemoration and no part of this row. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 15.08.2026 (2. август ст. ст.) — „Откриће и пренос моштију св. Стефана архиђакона и првомученика.“

attestations.note:
The day’s first of three entries. **THE DAY IS A FINDING AND A TRANSLATION OF RELICS AND THE ROW IS STILL WRITTEN, WHICH IS A READING AND NOT A HABIT.** §5 makes «Откриће и пренос моштију» a feast and therefore **no folder**, and no folder is made; what is written is a row on the folder this corpus already keeps, because the Prologue heads this day with him and quotes him in its own heading. The Julian 28 June met the same shape and could only add a note, the two saints there being venerated already; **this row was `undocumented`, so there was nothing to note and the choice was a row or nothing.** His passion is kept on 27 December by doxologia and saint.gr both, and **this book’s own 27 December was not opened** — it is outside this range, no page of it was fetched and nothing is claimed about what it prints. Whoever reads the Julian 12-27 will therefore find a venerated row on 2 August and owe a §4 second-day note arriving backwards, which is the `naum-of-ohrid` shape this wave already has on file. **AUTHOR: the alternative was to leave the row undocumented and report the day, and that is yours to prefer.** **NO NAME FORM, AND THE REASON IS GRAMMATICAL.** The heading gives his name only in the genitive, «св. Стефана архиђакона и првомученика», governed by моштију, and a case form is not a name form; nothing is stored and nothing is normalised by this reader. `types` untouched: архиђакон is `deacon` by §5 and the folder has it, and првомученик is `martyr`, which §5 states outright the corpus has no protomartyr type for and which the folder also has. **FOUR PERSONS IN THE BODY, EVERY ONE OF THEM REFUSED, AND ONE OF THEM IS KEPT BY ANOTHER CALENDAR ON THIS VERY DAY.** „Тело мучениково лежаше на отвореном месту под градом ноћ и два дана, а друге ноћи дође Гамалил, учитељ Павлов и потајни ученик Христов, узе тело, однесе га у Кафаргамалу на своје имање, и ту га чесно погребе у једној пећини.“ — Gamaliel, the teacher of Paul and a secret disciple of Christ, took the body by night to his estate at Kaphargamala and buried it in a cave; „У исту пећину сахрани Гамалил и свога пријатеља Никодима, који плачући над гробом Стефановим умре.“ buries his friend Nicodemus there, who died weeping over Stephen’s grave; „Ту сахрани Гамалил и свога крштенога сина Авива.“ buries his own baptised son Abibus; „И према своме завештању и сам Гамалил ту беше сахрањен.“ buries Gamaliel himself. **`gamaliel-the-teacher-of-the-law` is venerated by the Romanian calendar on this exact menologion day, 2/8** — and he is named in the body and not in the heading, so §5 gives him nothing, on the day after this same reader wrote his first `related` row ever. **And no `related` row is written to him here either**, on the corpus’s own ground: the carrying of a man’s relics is not a kinship (the Isidore ruling), and burying a body is that act and not a kinship. The teacher of Paul in this sentence is independent corroboration of the row written yesterday off the Julian 29 June, and it is recorded as that. Nicodemus, Abibus and the presbyter Lucian of Kaphargamala take no rows; `ls saints` holds no folder that is any of the three. **AND THE PATRIARCH WAS CAUGHT BY THE INSTRUMENT AND NOT BY THE EYE.** The draft paragraph first read «the patriarch John of Jerusalem», and `.tmp/sr-prosechk.mjs` reported `stephen-the-first-martyr -> john-of-jerusalem | NEEDS A ROW (forward false, back false)`: the corpus **does** keep a `john-of-jerusalem`, `Patriarch of Jerusalem`, on the Greek 30 March, and that three-word display name is a form `usableName` accepts. The row is refused — he is named in the body and not in the heading, and giving a blessing for a digging is not a relation — and whether the patriarch of 415 is that folder is an identification this reader did not make, so the sentence was rewritten to «the patriarch of Jerusalem, John», which the same instrument then reports clean. **NO `dates`.** „Но 415. год., за време Јерусалимског патријарха Јована, јави се Гамалил три пута у сну свештенику Кафаргамалском, Лукијану, и потанко му оприча све о сахрани свих поменутих указујући тачно место њихових заборављених гробова.“ gives **415** for the revelation to Lucian, and that is the year of a dream and a digging, not of a death: the corpus has no field for it, and `dates` on this folder is left exactly as it was. No `locations`: Kaphargamala, Sion and Constantinople are named in clauses. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion: the day carries the verse only, which is Bishop Nikolai’s own and belongs to no person. The ПЕСМА is twenty-eight lines, all of them on this entry and on nobody else of the day, and it is in no field and in no life (§3), read before this was written: „Усред ноћи тамне Гамалил се јави, Лукијану тајну чудесну објави; Гамалил се јави, старац достојанствен, На светломе лицу осмејак тајанствен, Дуга седа брада, и седе му власи, Хаљина му бела, црвен крст је краси.“ It then gives Gamaliel four beehives beside the four graves, three golden and one of silver, one filled with red flowers and three with white, which is a detail the prose does not carry at all.

SECOND-DAY NOTE, ADDED 8 OCTOBER 2026 BY THE READER OF THE JULIAN 27 DECEMBER, AND NOTHING ELSE UNDER THIS KEY WAS TOUCHED. The row above is carried back word for word — same day, same month, same source text, same url, same year, and the whole of the reading it came with — under `replace_venerated`, which BRIEF.md §4 sanctions for exactly this and nothing else. THE READING ABOVE SAID THIS WOULD ARRIVE AND NAMED ITS SHAPE CORRECTLY. The 27 December of this book, which that reader could not open, has now been read: the Охридски пролог for 27. децембар ст. ст., the civil 5 January read as `https://www.pravoslavno.rs/index.php?q=citanja&datum=2026-01-09&prolog=1`, and it heads the day with him, „Свети првомученик Стефан, архиђакон.“, over the fullest life on the page — a kinsman of the apostle Paul and a Jew of those Jews who lived in the Greek regions; the first of the seven deacons the apostles ordained for the helping of the poor at Jerusalem, which is why he was called archdeacon; great wonders by the power of his faith; the disputing Jews always beaten by his wisdom and by the power of the Spirit acting through him, who then stirred up the people and the elders with false witnesses; his face „као лице ангела“ as the book cites Acts 6:15; the speech that set out God’s benefits and the nation’s crimes and called them „издајницима и крвницима“; „Ево видим небеса отворена и Сина Човечјега гдје стоји с десне стране Бога“; the stoning outside the city; and that it happened A YEAR AFTER THE DESCENT OF THE HOLY SPIRIT ON THE APOSTLES. SO THE BOOK KEEPS HIM ON BOTH DAYS, the passion on 27 December and the finding and translation of the relics on 2 August. THE DAY IS NOT MOVED AND THE SECOND FEAST IS WRITTEN IN NO FIELD: one attestation row per church is the schema and §4 forbids changing the day under this key, so 27 December is recorded here and in the life and he does NOT render on the Serbian 27 December. OPEN FOR THE AUTHOR, AND NOW WITH BOTH PAGES READ: this corpus keeps his Serbian row on a translation of relics while his passion — the day the Romanian and the Greek both keep him on, and the day this same book heads with him and gives the life to — is 27 December. The 08-02 reader offered the alternative of leaving the row undocumented; the row exists, so the choice now is whether to move it, and moving it is the author’s act and not a reader’s. It is the `naum-of-ohrid` case of 12-23 exactly, two days apart in this same block. STILL NO NAME FORM, AND NOW FOR A DIFFERENT REASON. The 2 August heading gave the name only in the genitive and a case form is not a name form; THIS heading gives it in the nominative, «Стефан» — but the bare form was measured with `fk.mjs` before anything was written and it lands on THIRTEEN other folders (stefan-the-first-crowned, stephen-27-february, stephen-martyr-1937-4-september, stephen-monk-martyr-1937, stephen-monk-of-kazan-1918, stephen-of-khirsa, stephen-of-perm, stephen-of-vladimir, stephen-patriarch-of-constantinople, stephen-pope-of-rome, stephen-presbyter-martyr-1918-with-18, stephen-presbyter-martyr-1937-2-september-a, stephen-presbyter-martyr-1937-2-september-b), and the only other words in the heading are «првомученик» and «архиђакон», both RANKS, which §6 keeps out of a stored form. There was therefore no fuller form to write and a fourteen-member fold was refused instead — the 12-10 reader’s «Јован» refusal at eleven, at a higher count. `types` untouched: «првомученик» is `martyr` (§5 states the corpus has no protomartyr type) and «архиђакон» is `deacon`, and the folder carries both and `apostle` besides. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND NONE WRITTEN: the folder has none, and what this entry gives is not a year but a distance — one year after Pentecost — which is a span from an undated event and goes in no field. `related` UNTOUCHED: `paul-the-apostle` and `john-the-theologian` are both already there in both directions, and the entry names them both — Saul among his tormentors, and John the Theologian standing afar on a rock with the Most Holy Mother of God, who watched the martyrdom and prayed for him. ONE PERSON IN THIS BODY WAS REFUSED AGAIN, FOLLOWING THE 08-02 READER: «Гамалил, кнез јеврејски и потајни хришћанин», who took the body secretly and buried it on his own estate. The corpus DOES hold `gamaliel-the-teacher-of-the-law`, and the 2 August entry of this same book calls the man «учитељ Павлов», Paul’s teacher, which is that folder’s own description — so the identification is the book’s and not a guess. The 08-02 reader refused the row all the same and this reader does not overturn another reader’s refusal on the same book and the same man: the name stays in the book’s Cyrillic in the life, no link and no row is made in either direction, and IT IS NAMED IN THE REPORT AS ONE LINE OF WORK FOR THE AUTHOR. The Prologue prints no hymn on 27 December either.

hymns.text: Încununatu-s-a creștetul tău cu diademă împărătească, pe urma luptelor pe care le-ai pătimit pentru Hristos Dumnezeu, luptătorule cel dintâi printre mucenici. Că vădind nebunia iudeilor, ai văzut pe Mântuitorul tău, de-a dreapta Tatălui. Pe Acela roagă-L totdeauna pentru sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Apostol, Arhidiacon Ștefan, glasul 4

english.text: Your head was crowned with a royal diadem for the contests you endured for Christ God, first among the martyrs in the struggle; for having convicted the madness of the Jews, you saw your Saviour at the right hand of the Father. Pray to him always for our souls.

hymns.text: Βασίλειον διάδημα, ἐστέφθη σὴ κορυφή, ἐξ ἄθλων ὧν ὑπέμεινας, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ, Μαρτύρων Πρωτόαθλε· σὺ γὰρ τὴν Ἰουδαίων, ἀπελέγξας μανίαν, εἶδες σου τὸν Σωτῆρα, τοῦ Πατρὸς δεξιόθεν. Αὐτὸν οὖν ἐκδυσώπει ἀεί, ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Στέφανος ο Πρωτομάρτυρας και Αρχιδιάκονος», and it names him.

english.text: A royal diadem has crowned your head, out of the contests you endured for Christ God, first contender of the martyrs; for you, having confuted the madness of the Jews, saw your Saviour at the right hand of the Father. Entreat him, therefore, always, on behalf of our souls.

hymns.text: Ὁ Δεσπότης χθὲς ἡμῖν, διὰ σαρκὸς ἐπεδήμει, καὶ ὁ δοῦλος σήμερον, ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἐξεδήμει· χθὲς μὲν γάρ, ὁ Βασιλεύων σαρκὶ ἐτέχθη, σήμερον δέ, ὁ οἰκέτης λιθοβολεῖται· δι᾽ αὐτὸν καὶ τελειοῦται, ὁ Πρωτομάρτυς καὶ θεῖος Στέφανος.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — printed under «Άγιος Στέφανος ο Πρωτομάρτυρας και Αρχιδιάκονος», and it names him.

english.text: Yesterday the Master came to us in the flesh; today the servant departs out of the flesh. Yesterday he who reigns was born in the flesh; today the household servant is stoned. For his sake he is made perfect — the first martyr, the divine Stephen.
